description: Executioner series (1969-1980) are a men's action-adventure series written by Don Pendleton. They revolve around the central character, Mack Bolan, in a stylized, pulp fiction format, beginning with War Against the Mafiain 1969, and ending with Satan's Sabbathin 1980. After Satan's Sabbath, Pendleton licensed the rights to his Executioner characters to the Harlequin publishing group. After fifteen Executioner novels, Pendleton became involved in a legal battle with the publisher, Pinnacle Books, over ownership of the series. Pinnacle had the next entry, The Executioner #16: Sicilian Slaughter, written by an unknown writer under the pseudonym "Jim Petersen". Pendleton wrote what was published as #17, Jersey Guns, as his own sequel to # 15, Panic in Phillyunder a new contract with New American Library, which was ultimately voided by the terms of his settlement with Pinnacle, and he returned to the Bolan character for twenty-one more novels. title: The Executioner

description: LINKED WITH ALLURING INDULGENCE & COYOTE RIDGE Club Destiny, previously known as "Destined Hearts" prior to it's purchase in 2007 by Luke and Logan McCoy, is a prestigious Dallas nightclub that has become a sensation thanks in part to a series of events in recent years. Luke McCoy purchased the failing nightclub and renamed it Club Destiny because the original name sounded more like a dating website than a trendy nightclub. And in a matter of years, Luke and his silent partner - his twin brother Logan - established a trendy, booming downtown nightclub that rocks the doors off every night of the week. However, Club Destiny isn't all that it appears to be. Although there is a very legitimate nightclub that is open to the public, there is also a bigger secret hidden behind the locked doors. The membership list is long, even if the annual fee is more than some cars, but just because you can afford it, doesn't necessarily mean you'll get it.
